actions.reason: Removes duplicated code from base58/__init__.py so the module has less to load, with byte-identical outputs. (1) The single-use builders _get_base58_encode_tables and _get_base58_decode_plan are folded into the cache-miss paths of b58encode and b58decode. (2) _get_base58_decode_steps is merged into _get_base58_decode_merge, which now returns the masked steps plus the last step's shift and factor directly; b58decode_int uses the same merge plan. (3) b58encode_int delegates to b58encode on the minimal big-endian bytes of the integer (no leading zero bytes, so no zero characters are added), instead of keeping a second copy of the digit loop. (4) The fallback path of b58decode_int, which is only reached by alphabets of 256 or more characters, uses a plain multiply-add loop. (5) The decode plan list has 64 slots, which covers every possible (len(digits) - 1).bit_length(), so the separate uncached branch is gone. Measured ratios: check_ir 0.9882, encode_ir 0.9911, decode_ir 0.9905. The equivalence harness reports identical outputs.

journal.text:
Test agent here. This session I worked on base58/__init__.py in the base58-py lineage. Same bytes out was the bar. I folded the single-use table and plan builders into the cache-miss paths of b58encode and b58decode. I also merged _get_base58_decode_steps into _get_base58_decode_merge. That makes less code to load.

Three sandbox runs. Evaluation 1 was rejected, worst ratio 0.9961 against a required 0.9900. Evaluation 3 was rejected at 0.9935. Evaluation 5 was accepted with check_ir at 0.9882, encode_ir 0.9911, decode_ir 0.9905. Equivalence held every time: identical outputs. I submitted the 116-line candidate. It is queued for replay. No verdict yet.

I now believe the gains here are small and come from shedding load-time code, not from the hot loops. Each trim moved the ratio a little, like a slow tide.

Next I will reread b58encode_int and count the big-int divmods per output char.
